description: Add a repo-root allowlist .dockerignore so the cam-worker (.devcontainer) image build stops tarring the entire repo (4.9G seen in CAM-175) to the docker daemon.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms the allowlist idiom (* then ! re-include lines) and that the Dockerfile and .dockerignore are always sent to the builder even when excluded, so the bare * is safe with -f. Re-including a file nested under an excluded parent requires un-ignoring the parent directory first (the four-line form in this spec); BuildKit evaluates patterns last-match-wins.

userStories.title: Add allowlist .dockerignore for the cam-worker image build context
userStories.description: As a cam-cli developer running container mode, I need a repo-root .dockerignore that reduces the cam-worker image build context to the single COPYed file (.devcontainer/claude-config.json) so that docker build stops transferring gigabytes of node_modules, dist, .git, .claude logs, and orphan *.bun-build temps to the daemon on every build.
acceptanceCriteria: A .dockerignore exists at the repo root containing, in this exact relative order, the four allowlist lines: '*', '!.devcontainer', '.devcontainer/*', '!.devcontainer/claude-config.json'. [oracle: grep -Fxq '*' .dockerignore && grep -Fxq '!.devcontainer' .dockerignore && grep -Fxq '.devcontainer/*' .dockerignore && grep -Fxq '!.devcontainer/claude-config.json' .dockerignore]

The four lines are preceded by a header comment (lines starting with '#') that explains the ignore-all-but-one rule and states that any new Dockerfile COPY requires a matching re-include line or the build breaks. [oracle: grep -q '^#' .dockerignore && grep -qi 'COPY' .dockerignore]

A golden-fixture test asserts the .dockerignore content: the presence and exact relative order of the four allowlist lines and the presence of the header comment. [oracle: bun test test/dockerignore.test.ts]

docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile . still succeeds (the COPY of .devcontainer/claude-config.json resolves) and the transferred build context drops from gigabyte scale to kilobyte scale. Run where docker is available (macOS CI may lack docker); the reviewer or operator cites the 'transferring context' size line from the build log as the artifact of evidence. [oracle: DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile . ; reviewer cites the transferring-context size line]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: .dockerignore (new, repo root) and test/dockerignore.test.ts (new golden-fixture test; read via Bun.file, assert line order with indexOf comparisons or a full-content golden string). The .devcontainer/Dockerfile performs exactly one COPY (.devcontainer/claude-config.json -> /home/bun/.claude.json, line 89) and the workspace is bind-mounted at run time, so everything else in the context is wasted transfer. OUT OF SCOPE (do not do): denylist enumeration of individual artifacts, templating the .dockerignore into templates/ for downstream cam projects (cam-worker image is cam-cli internal; therefore NO embed-vendor:check needed), any change to the Dockerfile or the build command (buildDockerBuildArgv in src/supervisor/worker-container.ts stays untouched). Gotchas from the grill spec: (1) the re-include-nested-file idiom requires BuildKit last-match-wins evaluation; the legacy builder cannot re-include a file under an excluded parent; cam container-mode uses modern docker where BuildKit is default. (2) The .devcontainer directory must be un-ignored (!.devcontainer) before re-including the nested file; bare '*' plus a single nested re-include can fail on some builders, hence the four-line form. (3) The allowlist is brittle to a future Dockerfile COPY: the header comment must document that a new COPY requires a matching re-include line. (4) With -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile the Dockerfile is read directly, not from the context; docker docs also confirm Dockerfile/.dockerignore are always sent to the builder regardless, so excluding them via '*' is safe. Project rules: no em-dash in the persisted header comment; conventional commit (feat:). Related doc to re-check: docs/adr/0003-worker-isolation-boundary-dev-container.md (worker isolation boundary rationale for the dev-container image).
